issues.title: Symplecticity is overstated as an energy-conservation guarantee

failure_location.quote: In summary, our architecture maintains the symplectic structure of the original system, ensuring energy conservation and numerical stability through nonlinear transformations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: While our architecture inherently ensures symplecticity, exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced, as the proposed architecture only guarantees an approximate Hamiltonian is enforced.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that maintaining symplectic structure ensures energy conservation and numerical stability. The old methods section instead states that exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced and adds Hamiltonian behavior through a weighted training loss. Thus the old paper supports exact symplecticity together with promoted or penalized Hamiltonian consistency, not an unconditional energy-conservation guarantee; that difference is material.
issues.overall_effect: The contribution summary overstates a soft training objective and observed behavior as an architectural conservation guarantee; the underlying architecture and experiments are not invalidated by this prose defect.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the summary claim with a statement that the architecture preserves symplecticity by construction, while the Hamiltonian loss and training framework only promote Hamiltonian consistency and long-time stability; do not claim exact energy conservation or unconditional numerical stability.
issues.why_classification: The methods expressly state that exact Hamiltonian conservation is not enforced, so the original implication is a substantive overclaim rather than a transcription error. A local qualification resolves the issue without changing the method, but it withdraws coherent unconditional guarantees; this limited weakening exceeds a minor repair while avoiding global reconstruction.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: In summary, our architecture preserves the symplectic structure by construction and promotes Hamiltonian consistency and long-time numerical stability through the proposed nonlinear transformations and training framework.

issues.title: Universal-approximation theorem lacks an embedding-to-ambient reduction

failure_location.quote: The universal approximation capability of H\'enonNets implies that any symplectic diffeomorphism, including the nonlinear embedding defined above, can be approximated arbitrarily closely by composing a fixed linear embedding with H\'enonNet transformations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: they possess universal approximation properties for symplectic diffeomorphisms
Let $\Phi:\mathbb{R}^{2k}\to \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ be an arbitrary symplectic embedding defined on a compact domain $\Omega\subset \mathbb{R}^{2k}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For fixed Phi and compact Omega and each epsilon, the theorem requires uniform approximation of an arbitrary map from R^{2k} to R^{2n}. In the admissible regime k<n, such an embedding is rectangular, whereas the invoked H'enonNet capability is described in the old paper for full-dimensional symplectic diffeomorphisms. The old inference treats the embedding as if it were already an ambient diffeomorphism and supplies neither an ambient symplectic extension nor a factorization through the canonical inclusion. Thus the approximation conclusion is not established, although the symplecticity of an already constructed composition is unaffected.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem and the surrounding claim that a fixed canonical inclusion loses no approximation power are unsupported for general lower-dimensional symplectic embeddings.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a rigorous embedding-to-ambient factorization lemma, stating any required domain, symplectic-normal-bundle, and extension hypotheses, that gives an ambient symplectomorphism Psi with Phi = Psi composed with the canonical inclusion on Omega and places Psi within the scope of the cited H'enonNet approximation theorem. Then approximate Psi on the embedded compact set, derive exact symplecticity by composition, and conform the surrounding arbitrary-embedding and no-loss claims to the same scope.
issues.why_classification: Universality for full-dimensional symplectic diffeomorphisms cannot be applied directly to a rectangular embedding. Closing the gap requires a contained but nontrivial symplectic-neighborhood or extension argument, with its hypotheses checked, rather than a routine edit. A recognizably comparable universal-approximation result can survive without redesigning the architecture, so the issue is moderate rather than serious.

issues.title: Reconstruction MSE is overinterpreted as stability and convergence evidence

failure_location.quote: This superior performance of the hybrid approach demonstrates that G-reflector components enhance stability and accelerate convergence in linear wave problems, where prominent linear structures exist, the nonlinear H\'enonNet mapping benefits from supplementary linear symplectic corrections provided by G-reflectors.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Reconstruction MSE of training trajectories in Example~\ref{ex:linear-wave}.
Table \ref{tab:linear-rec} presents the MSEs of reconstruction across all training trajectories.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the hybrid model's lower reconstruction error demonstrates enhanced stability and accelerated convergence caused by G-reflectors. The old comparison actually establishes only reconstruction MSE over training trajectories; it reports neither a stability metric nor optimization or approximation convergence rates for the compared components. The claimed mechanism and performance dimensions therefore exceed what the table measures.
issues.overall_effect: The linear-wave comparison supports improved reconstruction fidelity but not the asserted stability or convergence benefits of the G-reflector component.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite the comparison to state only that the hybrid architecture attains the lowest reconstruction MSE on the reported training trajectories and that the G-reflector improves reconstruction fidelity in this experiment. Remove claims of enhanced stability, accelerated convergence, or a causal mechanism unless those properties are supported by dedicated metrics or convergence studies.
issues.why_classification: The table measures reconstruction error, not stability or convergence, so the unsupported performance dimensions cannot be retained through a routine same-guarantee correction. Restricting the prose to reconstruction fidelity is a local, complete, and recognizably comparable weakening, but it relinquishes substantive empirical claims and therefore exceeds a minor issue.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: For this linear wave problem, where strong linear structure is present, the additional linear symplectic corrections introduced by the G-reflector further enhance the effectiveness of the H\'enonNet-based nonlinear representation.

issues.title: Parametric-wave generator uses the wrong coefficient

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the wave speed parameter $\kappa(\omega)$ depends on a four-dimensional parameter vector $\omega=(\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3,\omega_4)$ via:

issues.failure_explanation: The example defines omega as a four-dimensional vector and kappa(omega) as the scalar wave coefficient. Both the PDE and the first-order equation use kappa(omega), but the displayed block of L uses omega squared. No scalar meaning for the square of this vector is supplied, and it does not reproduce the stated parameter dependence. The revised block uses the uniquely indicated coefficient kappa(omega).
issues.overall_effect: The printed semidiscrete matrix has an undefined or inconsistent parameter coefficient for the parametric wave example.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower-right block omega-squared times D_xx by kappa(omega) times D_xx in the displayed semidiscrete matrix L.
issues.why_classification: The old source defines omega as a vector and consistently uses the scalar kappa(omega) in the PDE, first-order system, and Hamiltonian. Those equations uniquely force the corrected coefficient, so the defect is a transcriptional inconsistency requiring no repair of the mathematical argument.

issues.title: Malformed cubic term in the nonlinear Schrödinger equation

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Introducing the real and imaginary variables via $u = p+ i q$, we obtain the canonical form

issues.failure_explanation: The old expression has an unclosed argument inside the first modulus and a final factor written as the real quantity |u| rather than u, so it is not the complex cubic nonlinearity represented by the subsequent canonical system. With u=p+iq, the displayed equations for p and q uniquely correspond to the term |u|^2u. The new version supplies exactly that term.
issues.overall_effect: The governing nonlinear Schrödinger equation is malformed and inconsistent with the canonical real system used immediately afterward.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the malformed nonlinear term by minus epsilon times |u(x,t,epsilon)| squared times u(x,t,epsilon), with the modulus and function arguments properly closed.
issues.why_classification: The subsequent real canonical system uniquely corresponds to the complex cubic term |u|^2u. Correcting the delimiters and final factor restores that uniquely forced expression without changing any inference, construction, or guarantee.
